chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said:
I asked Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the word of God the Exalted: 'The Beneficent is even upon the Throne' [20:5].

So he said: 'He is even with regard to everything. There is nothing closer to Him than another thing. The remote is not far from Him, and the close is not nearer to Him. He is even with regard to everything.'

key_terms.اسْتَوَى: istawaa - to be equal/even; the Imam interprets this not as 'sitting on' but as 'being equal with regard to' all things
key_terms.الْعَرْشُ: al-'Arsh - the Throne; in theological discourse, a symbol of God's sovereignty rather than a literal seat
key_terms.بَعِيدٌ: ba'id - the distant one; used to show that God is not further from distant things
key_terms.قَرِيبٌ: qarib - the close one; used to show that God is not nearer to nearby things

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Sadiq say about the Quranic verse 'The Beneficent is upon the Throne' (20:5)?
ai.summary: In this hadith, 'Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj asks Imam al-Sadiq (AS) about the Quranic verse 20:5, which describes God as 'established upon the Throne.' The Imam's response rejects any literal, anthropomorphic reading of the verse by explaining that God's 'istawaa' (being even/equal) signifies absolute spatial equality — He is equally present with all things, meaning no thing is closer or farther from Him than any other. This interpretation reflects the core Shia theological principle of tanzih (transcendence), asserting that God transcends all spatial categories and limitations. The early Muslim audience would have understood this as a definitive refutation of the Mujassima (corporealists), who claimed God literally sat on the Throne.

en.hubeali: And from him, from Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, from Safwan Bin Yahya, from Abdul Rahman Bin Al Hajjaj who said,
‘Abu Abdullahasws was asked about the Words of Allahazwj the Exalted [20:5] The Beneficent is Even upon the Throne.

So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Even with regards to everything. So there isn’t anything closer to Him<sup>azwj</sup> than a (another) thing. The remote is not far from Him<sup>azwj</sup>, and the close-by is not closer to Him<sup>azwj</sup>. He<sup>azwj</sup> is Even with regards to everything’.
en.sarwar: 8. Ali ibn Muhammad has narrated from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Safwan ibn Yahya from ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj from Imam abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.) the following about the words of Allah. “The Beneficent God is dominant over the Throne (of the realm).” [20:5] “No single thing is closer to Him than any other thing. The far is not far for Him and the close is not closer to Him. All are the same to Him.”
